confirmed.claim: Separating the 'replicate' action from 'refine/generate' is the correct and necessary adaptation that the AHD and AB-MCTS papers lack (design.md §4).
confirmed.evidence: Neither MCTS-AHD nor AB-MCTS has a repeat-measurement action (papers above); irace, SMAC and ParamILS treat repeated runs of the incumbent as essential.

confirmed.claim: Using the number of complete episodes, not truncated months, as the Hyperband/ASHA resource (mathematics.md §9; strategy-dossier.md §13).
confirmed.evidence: With complete episodes as the resource, Hyperband reduces to successive halving over replicates, a best-arm identification procedure (Karnin et al. 2013, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v28/karnin13.html). The late-benefit risk of greedy short-horizon selection is documented for PBT (FIRE-PBT, https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.13800).

confirmed.claim: Pending jobs are not observations, and decisions should use comparable rounds because short failures return first (mathematics.md §10).
confirmed.evidence: Standard asynchronous-race bias; essential when racing is combined with outcome-dependent episode duration.

confirmed.claim: The protocol §10 baselines (best-of-N without feedback, refine-leader, no reopening, target-only) are appropriate.
confirmed.evidence: AB-MCTS's own results show repeated sampling to be a strong baseline (https://arxiv.org/html/2503.04412v5).

confirmed.claim: PBT's checkpoint inheritance does not correspond to cloning game state (mathematics.md §8).
confirmed.evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.09846. With policies re-evaluated from fresh games, PBT degenerates into asynchronous truncation selection on single noisy evaluations, the failure mode surveyed by Jin & Branke 2005 (https://doi.org/10.1109/TEVC.2005.846356).

recommendations.recommendation: Rebuild the allocation core as batch-synchronous racing with incumbent intensification. Use irace-style elitist racing plus SMAC/ParamILS intensification, with top-two Thompson sampling or LUCB inside each round. The incumbent gets at least 2 fresh episodes every round, and a challenger can replace it only after matching a minimum run count and clearing a posterior threshold.
recommendations.rationale: This field was built for choosing among stochastic configurations under repeated looks. Re-evaluating the incumbent prevents the lucky-leader lock-in that single-evaluation evolutionary loops (ShinkaEvolve, AdaEvolve, GEPA minibatch acceptance) suffer under noise.

recommendations.recommendation: Replace the Hoeffding union-bound dormancy rule with variance-adaptive soft elimination (P(mu_i > mu_leader) < 0.10) during search. Pre-register an indifference zone: δ_screen = max(10 points, σ̂_cheap) on the cheap tier and δ_promote = 5 points on the target. Publish the resolution table: at σ=15, a 10-point difference needs about 36 episodes per arm and a 5-point difference about 142.
recommendations.rationale: The current band is ±44 points at n=30 and never separates candidates. Explicit indifference zones keep the team from spending the budget chasing ties smaller than the official 3-run noise (SE≈8.7 at σ=15).

recommendations.recommendation: Run a day-0 cost and variance pilot on the target (3 complete JiuwenSwarm episodes) and on the cheap tier (3-4 episodes), then apply decision rule D0. If the key budget covers 120 or more target episodes, rank on the target only. With 40-119, use two tiers plus an audit stream. Below 40, run no generative search on the target.
recommendations.rationale: Whether a proxy actor is needed at all depends on the unmeasured cost per target episode. Target-only evaluation removes problem A entirely if it is affordable.

recommendations.recommendation: Redefine the estimand and objective: per-run A = 0.8Q + 0.1TE_run (+0.1·D per version), with release decisions that maximise E[max(S_banked, S_new)]. Have a distinct strong candidate ready for R2 and for R3.
recommendations.rationale: Token efficiency is capped at 50 for early exits, and Stage 1 is the maximum over up to three released versions. Both change which candidate should be submitted and how much confidence a promotion needs.

recommendations.recommendation: Freeze each release candidate about 18 h before its cutoff and confirm it on fresh target episodes. Size confirmation as n_conf≈(1.28·σ̂/5)², about 15 at σ̂=15, capped by budget. Never reuse search data as confirmation.
recommendations.rationale: Selecting the best of several noisy candidates biases its estimate upward (optimizer's curse). Fresh data is the only cheap fix.

recommendations.recommendation: Evaluate the method against simple baselines at equal budget. Compare allocators by offline replay on a frozen catalogue: uniform, plain racing, successive halving, top-two TS, and our rule with and without incumbent re-evaluation and audit. Compare generation strategies in real cheap-tier runs: best-of-N without traces, best-of-N plus racing, always-refine-leader with parent re-evaluation, and the full method. Label the real runs as single-replicate pilots and report results at several budget points.
recommendations.rationale: Rankings of search strategies flip with the number of seeds and with budget. Replay gives many replicates at zero game cost for the allocation question.

recommendations.recommendation: Size candidate generation with an infinitely-many-armed rule: keep about ceil(√(round episode budget)) live candidates. Adapt to generator yield: halve new proposals if under 15% of new candidates reach P(beat incumbent) ≥ 0.3 after the first stage over two rounds, and increase them if over 40% do.
recommendations.rationale: This gives the progressive-widening exponent α=0.5 a theoretical anchor (K ∝ n^{β/(1+β)}, which is √n for β=1) and ties width to the generator's observed productivity rather than a fixed constant.

recommendations.recommendation: Run the cheap tier as an audited information source. Each round, promote the top-2 cheap candidates plus 1 uniformly random cheap-rejected candidate to the target. Revoke the cheap tier's elimination power if an audited reject reaches target P(better than the best promoted candidate) ≥ 0.5 in 2 of the first 4 audits. Keep the cheap harness close to JiuwenSwarm (same SKILL.md files and manifest instruction), and record actor as a model+harness pair.
recommendations.rationale: Multi-fidelity best-arm identification assumes a known bound on the cheap source's bias; here the bias is unknown and may reverse rankings. Auditing rejected candidates directly measures false rejections, which problem A requires.

recommendations.recommendation: Generate proposals from failure summaries aggregated over at least 3 episodes per parent. Apply a novelty filter (embedding plus an LLM judge asking 'would this change any decision?') and a compliance filter (no event answers or thresholds presented as rules). Trigger new families only when the last round produced no posterior-confirmed improvement.
recommendations.rationale: Diagnosing from one episode chases noise, and a near-duplicate wastes evaluation budget. ShinkaEvolve's novelty rejection is cheap and effective, and AdaEvolve-style meta-guidance needs a noise-robust trigger.

recommendations.recommendation: Correct the misreadings in the bibliography and design: AHC058 operators, the scope of ShinkaEvolve's ablations, AB-MCTS's loss to repeated sampling, the HOO/StoSOO partition structure, AdaEvolve's absent theory and single-evaluation signal, EvoTest's UCB and its AUC objective, and BAST at UAI 2007.
recommendations.rationale: The expert review rewards accurate attribution of known mechanisms versus the team's own adaptation.

recommendations.recommendation: If a behavioural archive is kept, estimate its descriptors and elite values from replicated episodes, in the manner of uncertain quality-diversity, rather than from single draws.
recommendations.rationale: MAP-Elites is known to fail in uncertain domains when elites are chosen on single noisy evaluations.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not adopt Track-and-Stop, PBT or full Bayesian VOI/knowledge-gradient as the allocator this week. Cite them as the asymptotically optimal or idealised references, and use top-two TS or LUCB, whose behaviour is good at small n.
recommendations.rationale: Track-and-Stop's optimality is asymptotic for a fixed arm set. PBT degenerates to single-evaluation truncation selection. VOI needs a generative model of the mutation operator that we do not have.

audit.concrete_protocol:
RELEASE-ALIGNED GENERATE-AND-RACE (GAR). Tags: [K] = known mechanism, [A] = team adaptation.

0. UNITS AND ESTIMAND
- Cell = (policy hash, actor+harness, runner/engine/dataset version). Statistics are kept per cell and never pooled across actors [A].
- Unit = one episode run to genuine termination, which may be an early game elimination.
- Operational failure (tool crash, rate limit, harness bug): the episode is re-queued and logged, never scored and never counted as zero. A cell with more than 10% operational failures is flagged [A].
- Per-run outcome A = 0.8·Q + 0.1·TE_run, with TE_run under the published rule (100 at ≤500k tokens/month, linear to 0 at 3M, capped at 50 for an early exit). D, the Skill quality, is a per-version rubric estimate used for tie-breaks and release sums [A].
- Auxiliary metrics: Q, P(reach month 48), survival months, tokens/month, invalid actions and tool errors.
- Model: A_i ~ N(μ_i, σ_i²) with a Normal-Inverse-Gamma posterior. σ_i² is shrunk toward the pooled σ̂² (4 pseudo-observations). A nonparametric bootstrap is reported alongside, because outcomes are bimodal (early exit vs completion).

1. DAY 0: PILOT AND REGIME CHOICE (26-27 Oct)
- Target pilot: 3 complete episodes of the R1 candidate in JiuwenSwarm 0.2.4b3, mode agent, designated model. Measure cost per target episode (c_T), wall time, errors and σ̂.
- Cheap pilot: 3-4 episodes of the same Skills in the cheap harness.
- Decision D0: N_T = floor(0.85·remaining key budget / c_T).
  - N_T ≥ 120: target-only racing. Claude workers are used only to debug execution and produce traces.
  - 40 ≤ N_T < 120: two tiers plus an audit stream.
  - N_T < 40: no generative search on the target; at most 2-3 hand-designed candidates with at least 8 target episodes each.
- R1 (cutoff 27 Oct 24:00): submit the candidate that ran cleanly, preferring lower variance. The goal is to bank a valid score.

2. GENERATION, PER ROUND (orchestrator Opus)
- Input: failure summaries aggregated over at least 3 episodes per parent, the current posteriors, and the archive table [A].
- Proposal mix:
  - 50% single-hypothesis diffs of the top-2 policies by posterior mean (GEPA/ReEvo reflective mutation [K]).
  - 25% diffs of other families, with parents sampled in proportion to P(best), not argmax (ShinkaEvolve weighted sampling / GEPA frontier [K]).
  - 25% a new family or a reopened dormant candidate; one slot is reserved for reopening at least every second round, taking the oldest under-sampled (n<8) dormant candidate or one with a new hypothesis [K/A].
- New-family trigger: the previous round produced no candidate with P(beat incumbent) ≥ 0.5. This is AdaEvolve-style meta-guidance on posteriors rather than single draws [A].
- Filters:
  - Compliance: no named-event answers, and no thresholds presented as rules.
  - Novelty: embedding similarity plus an LLM judge asking "does it change any decision?" (ShinkaEvolve [K]).
  - Capability: a length/complexity cap for the target actor.
- Width: live candidates L ≈ ceil(√B_r), where B_r is the episode budget of the round (infinitely-many-armed rule, β≈1; equal to MCTS-AHD's α=0.5 [K]).
- Yield adaptation [A]: yield y = fraction of new candidates with P(beat incumbent) ≥ 0.3 after the first stage. If y < 0.15 for two rounds, halve the number of new candidates and shift budget to replication. If y > 0.4, raise it.

3. ALLOCATION, PER ROUND (irace elitist racing + SMAC/ParamILS intensification + top-two TS [K])
- First stage: n0 = 4 episodes per new candidate on its tier (3 on target-only if N_T < 120).
- The incumbent receives ≥ 2 fresh episodes every round (parent re-evaluation, noisy-EA [K]).
- Batch-synchronous: no decision until every launched episode in the batch is terminal or classified as operational. Long successful games are waited for, which prevents the asynchronous duration bias against late-benefit policies (problem B) [A].
- Soft elimination to dormant: P(μ_i > μ_leader) < 0.10, reversible.
- Remaining round budget: top-two Thompson sampling (β=0.5) among non-dormant candidates. When m distinct release candidates are needed, use LUCB-style top-m: sample the weakest member of the top m and the strongest outsider [K].
- Incumbent change, on the target tier only: n_i ≥ min(n_inc, 10) and P(μ_i > μ_inc) ≥ 0.80 [K/A].
- Pre-registered indifference zones: δ_screen = max(10, σ̂_cheap) and δ_promote = 5 points. Differences inside δ are declared ties and broken by D, tokens/month and simplicity [K/A].
- No truncation pruning. Month-12/24 proxies are logged only to test their validity after the week [A].

4. FIDELITY (two-tier regime only) [A on K]
- The cheap tier may only:
  - flag execution failures;
  - set dormancy at δ_screen;
  - generate traces.
- Each round, promote to the target with n0_T = 3: the top-2 cheap candidates plus 1 uniformly random cheap-dormant candidate (the audit).
- Revocation: if an audited reject reaches target P(μ_audit > μ_best_promoted) ≥ 0.5 in 2 of the first 4 audits, the cheap tier loses elimination power.
- Report the false-rejection rate with a Clopper-Pearson interval. Recalibrate whenever a new family enters.

5. SPECIALISATION (problem C)
- Every specialist is evaluated as a complete policy against its parent from fresh games.
- Each calendar-triggered variant is paired with a state-triggered variant.
- A specialist is kept only if it beats both its parent and its counterpart on fresh episodes.

6. FREEZE, CONFIRM, RELEASE [K + A]
- Freeze about 18 h before the R2 (30 Oct) and R3 (1 Nov) cutoffs.
- Confirmation: n_conf ≈ (1.28·σ̂/5)², about 15 at σ̂=15, capped by budget. Use fresh target episodes only, never search data (optimizer's curse).
- Release rule: submit the distinct candidate that maximises the Monte Carlo value of E[max(S_banked, S_new)]. S_new = 0.8·mean of 3 posterior-predictive draws + 0.1·TE + 0.1·D̂. S_banked is the official R1/R2 score if it has arrived, otherwise the local estimate.
- When several candidates are confirmed at once, apply Holm across the reported claims. If confirmation is monitored while it runs, use a betting confidence sequence.
- Whether a lower-scoring later version harms the expert review is an open organiser question (Q8).

7. METHOD EVALUATION AT EQUAL BUDGET
- (a) Allocators, by offline replay at zero game cost. Take the frozen catalogue of candidates with at least 8 episodes each and run 10,000 bootstrap replicates at budgets B ∈ {30, 60, 120}. Compare uniform allocation, plain racing (Welch, α=0.1), successive halving, top-two TS, and GAR with and without incumbent re-evaluation and audit. Metrics: P(selected within 5 points of the best) and simple regret.
- (b) Generation, by real cheap-tier runs with an equal budget of about 60 episodes each:
  - B1: best-of-N, with N≈15 proposals from the seed prompt, no traces, uniform n0=4.
  - B2: B1 plus racing.
  - B3: always-refine-leader, a (1+1) loop with reflective mutation, parent re-evaluation and acceptance at P > 0.8.
  - B4: plain racing over a fixed hand-written catalogue with no generation.
  - B5: full GAR.
  Each final pick receives the same target confirmation. These are single replicates, reported as a pilot at several budget points (rankings flip with seeds and budget).
- (c) Ablations, only if budget remains after R3: reopening quota 0 vs 10%; audit off (by replay); single-family (no diversity); no context modes.

KNOWN VS ADAPTATION
- Known mechanisms: racing and elimination; incumbent intensification; top-two TS and LUCB; successive halving; KN indifference zones; confidence sequences; reflective trace mutation; novelty rejection; archives; progressive widening via infinitely-many-armed sizing; parent re-evaluation and resampling; fresh holdout confirmation.
- Team adaptations:
  - actor+harness cells with an audit-based revocation rule;
  - batch-synchronous racing against duration-correlated arrival;
  - the composite per-run estimand with the TE cap;
  - release-aligned top-m selection with a max-over-releases decision rule;
  - stagnation triggers on posteriors, not single draws;
  - offline replay to compare allocators.
failure_evidence: The pilot shows σ̂ ≥ 20 points and c_T ≥ USD 1: under 45 target episodes are possible, nothing below a 15-point gap can be resolved, and generative search on the target should be abandoned.
An audited cheap-rejected candidate beats the cheap-promoted candidates on the target in 2 or more of the first 4 audits: cheap-tier ranking is unreliable for pruning (problem A materialises).
After each incumbent change, the new incumbent's mean on its re-evaluation episodes falls by more than 1 SE: the promotion thresholds are admitting winner's-curse picks.
Fresh confirmation means fall systematically below selection-phase means by more than 1 SE: the optimizer's curse is not being controlled; raise n0 or lower the number of live candidates.

Generator yield stays under 0.15 for two rounds, or the novelty filter rejects over 50% of proposals: the generator is unproductive, so switch to plain racing over hand-designed families (baseline B4).
Offline replay shows GAR allocation no better than uniform allocation or successive halving at equal budget: drop the extra complexity.

The official R1 score (3-run mean) lies more than 2 official SEs below the local target estimate for the same version: there is a dev-vs-official environment shift, and local precision is not transferring.
Operational interruptions exceed 10% or correlate with policy family: the censoring threatens the comparability of cells.
Candidates diverge mainly on early exits while their completed-run scores are similar: the TE cap and survival dominate, and the estimand weights should be re-checked.
open_questions: What does one complete target episode cost in USD and wall time under the organiser-routed deepseek-v4-flash, and what is σ of A for reasoned policies? Neither has been measured; the random baseline reports a mean of 11.8 and a max of 28.9 but no SD.
Do the organisers permit Claude-driven development workers, deterministic scripted drivers and parallel dev sessions? See organiser-questions.md A1-A2; no permission is established.

When Stage 1's maximum comes from an earlier version, which version's Skills, design documents and video go to expert review? This decides whether submitting a distinct candidate at R2 and R3 is free.
Does the official evaluation environment use parameters or event composition shifted from dev? If so, local precision finer than about 5 points buys little.

Is session state isolated when several stdio servers run concurrently, given the runner's shared career_emulator.sqlite3 and the CLI's competition mode, which allows only one new game? This must be checked through the documented interface only.
Does OpenRouter upstream routing add run-to-run variance in official scoring that is absent from dev runs?
Can the cheap harness (Claude Code CLI with MCP) present Skills exactly as JiuwenSwarm does? If not, how large is the harness effect, as opposed to the model effect, on rankings?

verdicts.reason: The arithmetic reproduces exactly from mathematics.md §4 lines 48-52 with delta=0.05 and delta_i=6delta/(pi^2 i^2). For i=1 the half-widths are ±68.2 (n=10), ±43.8 (n=30) and ±26.4 (n=100). For i=10 they are ±83.4, ±51.8 and ±30.4. The from-zero-lab §5A K=4 formula (line 77) gives ±71.3 and ±45.4. Hoeffding uses the range, so its variance proxy is a 50-point SD. The 142 and 36 per-arm figures are the standard two-sample sizes at two-sided alpha=0.05, power 0.8 and sigma=15. Part of the auditor's framing overstates the prior text. Line 54 already calls the rule 'una derivación ilustrativa, no la implementación más eficiente', concedes that it may eliminate nothing, and names empirical-Bernstein and mixture confidence sequences (Howard et al.) as better. from-zero-lab line 77 says 'su rigor no crea información'. The core defect stands: line 56 is the only formal dormancy rule anywhere in the spec (lab-spec.json defines none), and it is inoperative even at n=100, not merely 'con pocas muestras'. 'Allocation silently becomes uniform' is speculation, because the spec defines no allocator that would fall back to uniform. Severity is moderate, since the text flags the rule as illustrative.
verdicts.refined_correction: Mark the Hoeffding/union-bound band as a non-operative illustration. Make the normative dormancy rule variance-adaptive and reversible. One option is a Bayesian soft elimination such as P(mu_i > mu_leader) < 0.10 under a Normal model with variance shrunk to the pooled estimate, reported with a whole-episode bootstrap because outcomes may be bimodal. Another is a fully sequential indifference-zone procedure (Kim & Nelson 2001, doi:10.1145/502109.502111). For anytime-valid confirmation monitoring, use betting or predictable-plug-in empirical-Bernstein confidence sequences (Waudby-Smith & Ramdas 2024, doi:10.1093/jrsssb/qkad009). Do not use the Maurer-Pontil form: its range term is still about ±30 points or more at n=30. Publish the resolution table as a function of the measured SD, not a fixed sigma=15. The random-policy data (scores 3.1-28.9, mean 11.8) cannot inform the SD of reasoning policies. Early-exit/completion bimodality could push sigma to 25-30, which multiplies the required n by about 3-4.

verdicts.reason: The paper facts are mostly accurate, but the prior text already makes the correction. The README (line 7) restricts MCTS-AHD/AB-MCTS to deciding 'dónde generar variantes' and assigns allocation of episodes to separate 'comparaciones secuenciales'. The README table row 'Separar generación de candidatos de medición repetida' does the same. bibliography R01 says max backup is 'not a calibrated estimator for noisy game episodes', and R02 says 'a GEN node is not an ordinary fixed arm'. mathematics.md §3 and findings.md line 18 both say MCTS-AHD's max backup must not be copied under episode noise. protocol.md §10 already lists best-of-N as a baseline. Only the wording 'closely matches' in findings.md line 7 is loose. The auditor's AB-MCTS evidence is also selective. Table 1 (arXiv 2503.04412v5) does show repeated sampling ahead on ARC-AGI at 128 calls (15.0 vs 12.3 with GPT-4o; 18.6 vs 16.0 with DeepSeek-V3). However, AB-MCTS-M has the best average rank (2.3 vs 3.5). It beats repeated sampling clearly on CodeContest with GPT-4o (40.6±1.0 vs 37.9±0.3). Section 4.3 reports that at budgets up to 512 calls on ARC-AGI, AB-MCTS 'ultimately achieves performance levels that repeated sampling cannot reach'. The MCTS-AHD details check out: PW floor(N^0.5) >= |children|, max backup, T=1000, 64 TSP50 instances, no SDs. The paper is internally inconsistent on run counts (5, 10 or 3), so '5 runs' is imprecise.
verdicts.refined_correction: Cosmetic fix only. Change findings.md line 7 from 'closely matches the proposed outer policy tree' to 'is the closest precedent for organising generated candidates in a tree with progressive widening and retention of weak candidates; it scores each node once on a fixed instance set and gives no guidance on replicated stochastic evaluation'. Keep best-of-N as a first-class equal-budget baseline, as protocol §10 already does. Cite AB-MCTS's mixed result accurately: it loses to repeated sampling on ARC-AGI at 128 calls, surpasses it at 512 calls, and has the best average rank in Table 1.

verdicts.reason: The core omission is real. The selected 55-source bibliography (R19-R39) contains no algorithm-configuration or racing literature (Hoeffding races, F-Race, irace, ParamILS, SMAC intensification). It also lacks indifference-zone ranking and selection (KN), LUCB, successive rejects, sequential halving, noisy-EC re-evaluation and the optimizer's curse. These are the fields built for choosing among noisy, expensive configurations. completion-audit row 1 nonetheless claims the matching methods were identified. Track-and-Stop appears only as unselected candidates in search-audit.json (lines 551 and 576). The auditor's grep evidence is partly wrong, though, because it searched only in English. from-zero-lab.md line 73 explicitly describes round-based racing: 'una carrera sencilla por rondas es suficiente: probar todos, retirar los claramente inferiores, repetir los que siguen compitiendo'. Hyperband and ASHA (R29-R30) are successive-halving algorithms. followup-search-audit.md lists Gabillon et al. 2012 (UGapE), a ranking-and-selection review and knowledge-gradient papers as unselected leads. The statement 'no mention of racing or successive halving' is therefore false. The omission is of the algorithm-configuration and ranking-and-selection literature and its mechanisms (elitist racing, incumbent intensification, indifference zones), not of the concept. The cited references check out: irace ORP 3:43-58; ParamILS JAIR 36; LUCB ICML 2012; Karnin et al. ICML 2013; Jin & Branke TEVC 2005; TRIPLE (Shi et al., NeurIPS 2024); Poiani et al. NeurIPS 2022, which assumes known maximal bias per fidelity.
verdicts.refined_correction: Keep from-zero-lab's round-based racing as the starting point and ground it in the canonical sources. Add Maron & Moore 1993, Birattari et al. 2002 and López-Ibáñez et al. 2016 (irace: elitist iterated racing). Add Hutter et al. 2009 and 2011 (ParamILS/SMAC intensification, where a challenger must match the incumbent's run count). Add Kim & Nelson 2001 and Nelson et al. 2001 (indifference-zone and screen-then-select). Add Kalyanakrishnan et al. 2012 (LUCB, top-m), Audibert et al. 2010 and Karnin et al. 2013 (fixed budget), Jin & Branke 2005 (parent re-evaluation under noise) and Smith & Winkler 2006 (optimizer's curse). Shi et al. 2024 (TRIPLE) is the closest prompt-specific precedent. Poiani et al. 2022 is useful mainly as a contrast, because it assumes a known bias bound we do not have. Infinitely-many-armed and uncertain-QD papers are optional. Correct completion-audit row 1 so it no longer claims full coverage.

verdicts.reason: Verified in competition-rules.rst.txt. Lines 185-198 say token efficiency is scored per run from total_tokens/survival_months and averaged over the three runs, and that 'A run that ends before month 48 is capped at 50 on this term'. At equal Q, a completion can therefore be worth up to 0.1×50 = 5 automated points more than an early exit. Lines 96-97 and 334-342 make Stage 1 the highest valid version score across the two interim releases and the final release, and a lower later score does not reduce it. Lines 321-325 say only the latest unscored version is evaluated per cutoff. Lines 327-332 say content-identical versions are not rescored, so a new official draw requires a substantively distinct version. mathematics.md §1 lines 9-15 define Y = Q/100 and single-policy simple regret. Line 19 says optimising mu is only a component, but it does not repair the estimand. lab-spec.json sets primary_outcome to the mean terminal quantitative_score. Other repo files already know these facts: budget-and-search.md line 57 (TE cap), strategy-dossier.md lines 25, 32 and 213 (max retention, duplicates do not buy rolls) and organiser-questions Q8. The hierarchical-lab objective simply fails to integrate them. Part of the auditor's correction is shaky. Distinctness follows from the content-identical rule, not from top-m theory. A refined, substantively changed version of the leader is a legitimate distinct candidate, so formal top-m identification is not required.
verdicts.refined_correction: Use a per-run primary estimand A = 0.8Q + 0.1·TE_run, computed only in target-harness cells, because Claude-worker token counts are not comparable to JiuwenSwarm+deepseek. Estimate 0.1·D per version from a rubric, and keep Q, P(month 48) and tokens/month as auxiliaries. On the cheap tier, rank on Q and completion only. At R2 and R3, choose the version that maximises a Monte Carlo estimate of E[max(S_banked, S_new)]. Treat S_banked as uncertain until the official score arrives, and model S_new as 0.8 × the mean of 3 posterior-predictive draws plus the TE and D terms. Note that this objective rewards variance, which should be weighed against the 30% expert review for top-10 teams and the open organiser question Q8. The new version must not be content-identical to a scored one (rules lines 327-332). A substantively improved descendant of the leader qualifies; formal top-m identification is optional.

verdicts.reason: design.md §14 faithfully summarises what ShinkaEvolve reports. Its Section 5 says 'Hill climbing shows strong initial performance but plateaus quickly, while weighted sampling maintains steady improvement throughout evolution'. The Fig. 9 caption reads 'Weighted parent sampling outperforms random search and hill climbing', and the takeaways claim it 'consistently outperforms both random search and hill climbing'. Weighted sampling is a diversity-preserving parent-selection rule, so 'favorecen conservar diversidad frente a ascender siempre al líder' is not a misreading. The scope caveat is valid but missing: the ablation is on circle packing only, seeds and error bars are not reported, and evaluation is single and seeded. The auditor's inference that 'at this week's budget we are in the early regime, where the cited evidence favours greedy refinement' is unsupported. The paper reports no crossover generation that maps to our candidate counts, and hill climbing's early advantage was measured with a noise-free single evaluation. Under episode noise, a hill-climber locks onto a lucky leader unless the parent is re-evaluated. The auditor's own correction is already in the protocol: §10 lists 'Refinar siempre al líder' as a comparator and §11 ablates archive diversity separately. The GEPA Table 3 numbers the auditor cites are correct (Pareto 61.28 vs SelectBestCandidate 54.89, Qwen3-8B, four tasks), and they support the prior position.
verdicts.refined_correction: Add a scope caveat to design.md §14: 'ShinkaEvolve's parent-selection ablation is reported for circle packing only, with single seeded evaluations and no stated seed count; GEPA's Pareto-vs-best ablation (Table 3) is stronger evidence but relies on a shared validation set.' Keep always-refine-leader as a baseline, as protocol §10 already does, and add parent re-evaluation to it. Treat archive diversity as an ablated component, as §11 already does. Do not claim that the evidence favours greedy refinement at small budgets.

GAR launches Claude-subscription workers and automated JiuwenSwarm target batches without the organiser-clarification gate the prior research treats as blocking (README 'Restricción decisiva', protocol §1, lab-spec gates, organiser-questions). The binding rules say that when the rules are silent, the team must ask before using a method. Day 0 should start with that gate, and the cheap tier should be dropped if no written clarification arrives. GAR also never budgets Claude Max 5-hour and weekly limits (findings.md records extra usage disabled), which may cap the cheap tier far below 300+ episodes.

Fixed constants. The D0 thresholds (120 and 40 episodes), n0=4, at least 2 incumbent episodes per round, min(n_inc,10), 2-of-4 audits, 15% and 40% yield cut-offs, 4 pseudo-observations and an 18 h freeze are all fixed. The project explicitly requires sample sizes driven by observed variability. Derive the regime threshold from the measured SD, the per-episode target cost c_T and delta_promote, for example N_needed = k·n(delta_promote, sigma_hat) + n_conf. Realistically, at USD 50 and up to 24M tokens for a 48-month run at the TE full-mark boundary, N_T is likely below 40. The plan should therefore be designed primarily for that regime, not treat it as a fallback.

Too few rounds for the multi-round rules. Batch-synchronous rounds of full 48-month episodes over about 6 days allow only a handful of rounds. Rules that need several rounds of evidence may never fire before R3: yield over two rounds, revocation 'in 2 of the first 4 audits', and a reopening slot every second round. With one audit per round, 4 audits give a Clopper-Pearson interval of roughly [0.006, 0.81] for 1/4, which is uninformative. One random cheap-rejected candidate at n0_T=3 cannot reach a reliable P >= 0.5 of beating the best promoted candidate. Use the shared-policy calibration matrix plus audits stratified toward candidates the cheap tier rejected narrowly.

Batch-synchronous timeouts and problem B. 'No decision until every episode is terminal or classified operational' needs a timeout policy. A timeout set near typical durations would mislabel long, late-benefit successful games as operational failures, which reintroduces the duration bias it is meant to prevent. Set timeouts far above the maximum plausible duration, and resume by observing the session rather than aborting. The protocol also does not address session isolation. The runner writes a shared career_emulator.sqlite3, and '-c' competition mode allows only one new game, so parallel batches need verified isolation through documented options (prior protocol §4).

The release rule over-reaches. E[max(S_banked, S_new)] rewards variance, which conflicts with the 30% expert review for top-10 teams while organiser question Q8 is open. The real Stage 1 stake is rank and P(top 10), not the expected maximum. Distinctness is forced by the content-identical rule (rules lines 327-332), not by top-m theory, and a substantively refined leader descendant is a legitimate distinct version. TE_run on Claude-worker cells is meaningless because the token counts are not comparable to the target harness; compute TE only in target cells.

Real-run search comparisons B1-B5. Five arms at about 60 cheap episodes each is roughly 300 episodes of single-replicate comparisons, which have near-zero inferential value. The auditor's own citation (Oved et al., arXiv 2609.19799, 'the strategy that looks worst at one seed is best at forty seeds') and prior protocol §10 ('La unidad externa de replicación es una búsqueda completa') imply exactly this. Spend that budget on the actual search. Keep only the zero-cost allocator replay, and state that replay treats the catalogue's bootstrap distribution as ground truth.

Confirmation sizing. n_conf ≈ (1.28·sigma_hat/5)^2 ≈ 15 fresh target episodes inside an 18 h freeze is not checked against measured wall time per episode, rate limits or key cost. At plausible costs it could consume a third or more of the USD 50 key per release. Size it by c_T and wall time, and accept a wider precision target when necessary rather than skipping freezing.

Recommendation 10 contains its own misreading. It calls for correcting the bibliography on 'AB-MCTS's loss to repeated sampling', but no prior repo text claims AB-MCTS beats best-of-N. In Table 1, AB-MCTS-M has the best average rank (2.3 vs 3.5) and clearly beats repeated sampling on CodeContest. Section 4.3 reports that AB-MCTS surpasses repeated sampling on ARC-AGI at budgets up to 512 calls. It trails only on ARC-AGI at 128 calls.

Inconsistent evidence standard in recommendation 9. It cites ShinkaEvolve's novelty rejection as 'cheap and effective' from the same circle-packing ablation the auditor discounts in error 4. The paper itself reports that the LLM novelty judge adds only marginal gains, and embedding similarity on code does not transfer directly to natural-language policies. Treat the novelty filter as a cheap heuristic, not as evidence-backed.

The infinitely-many-armed 'theoretical anchor' in recommendation 7 is overstated. The Wang, Audibert & Munos and Carpentier & Valko results assume i.i.d. draws from a fixed reservoir with a known or estimated beta. LLM proposals conditioned on feedback and parents violate that assumption. Equating it to MCTS-AHD's per-node visit-based widening rule (alpha=0.5) is an analogy, not a derivation. sqrt(B_r) is fine as a heuristic default but should not be presented as theory-backed.

Normal-Inverse-Gamma soft elimination at n=3-4. With bimodal early-exit versus completion outcomes, P(mu_i > mu_leader) < 0.10 can be miscalibrated at these sample sizes. Pre-register a minimum n before any elimination, and check the bootstrap against the Normal posterior before letting it drive dormancy.

audit.dimension: Problem A: worker capability and bias (multi-fidelity, cross-model transfer between Claude/scripted workers and deepseek-v4-flash in JiuwenSwarm)
audit.verdict_summary: The qualitative principles in the research are sound. Estimands are actor-specific (mu_model(policy)). Actors are never pooled as IID. A cheap source must be calibrated before it may prune. Discarded candidates are audited on the target. Fidelity can depend on the input (iMFBO). There are no mid-episode actor switches. A target-only comparator appears in the method evaluation, and the 'measure on target first if the cheap source is unvalidated' rule is in mathematics.md section 5. Problem A is still not operationalised. Nothing is pre-registered: no thresholds, no estimators, no audit sampling design, no sample-size logic. The 6 policies x 2 actors x 3 episodes pilot cannot establish ranking agreement: with K=6 policies the 95% CI for an observed r=0.8 is about [-0.03, 0.98] even if every cell mean were measured perfectly. The research omits multi-fidelity best-arm identification, prediction-powered inference and control-variate theory. Most importantly, it never states that episode-level variance reduction between actors is impossible here, because nothing pairs a cheap episode with a target episode (no seeds, no cloning). It also misses the one pairing that is available: decision-level replay of logged contexts. The core premise that the Claude workers are the 'cheap' tier is unverified and probably wrong per token. OpenRouter's deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash costs about $0.05-0.60/M input across 17 endpoints. Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10/M, rising to $0.50/M for requests over 100k tokens, and Sonnet 5.5 costs $2/M. The account actually uses a Claude Max subscription, where the binding limits are usage windows, not dollars. The target actor itself is underspecified. The OpenRouter slug currently resolves to 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0423', served at fp4, fp8 or mxfp4 depending on provider. DeepSeek's own API now serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 under the retired name. So 'self-funding deepseek-v4-flash' through DeepSeek's API would silently test a different model. Three things are not addressed: the harness gap between Claude Code and JiuwenSwarm; the rule-compliance risk of a Claude Code worker that keeps its filesystem tools; and length-biased censoring caused by subscription limits. Finally, the design assumes Haiku is the weaker executor and treats Sonnet as an escalation arm. A stronger Claude actor may instead mask under-specified Skills and compress the differences between policies. Overall: correct cautions, missing machinery, and a resource premise that should be inverted to target-model-first.

Fisher-z 95% intervals for an observed correlation of 0.8 between perfectly measured policy means are [-0.03, 0.98] at K=6, [0.42, 0.94] at K=12 and [0.55, 0.92] at K=20. With 3 episodes per cell, the reliability of cell means is s_b^2/(s_b^2 + sigma^2/n): 0.16 when the between-policy SD is 5 and the episode SD is 20, and 0.75 when they are 10 and 10. The section is honestly labelled 'not a power justification', but nothing links it to a gate, so whether Haiku may prune is left to interpretation.

errors.location: research/hierarchical-lab/mathematics.md section 7 (lines 90-110); bibliography.md 'Contexto y transferencia' and R33-R35
errors.claim: A provisional calibration mu_target(p) = a_m(x_p) + b_m(x_p)*mu_m(p) + residual, with rMFBO and iMFBO as the supporting literature.
errors.problem: The literature that actually governs this decision is missing, and so is the consequence that matters most. (1) Multi-fidelity best-arm identification (Kandasamy et al. 2016; Poiani et al. 2022, 2024) assumes a known maximum bias for each fidelity. The lab has no bias bound, so any pruning rule must estimate one and carry its uncertainty. (2) PPI, PPI++, active and stratified PPI, control variates, multi-fidelity Monte Carlo and Kennedy-O'Hagan co-kriging all gain only from correlation between proxy and gold measured on the same unit. Cheap and target episodes are independent here (no seeds, no cloning), so episode-level control variates and PPI give zero variance reduction. Policy-level PPI++ gains at most a factor of 1/(1-rho^2): 1.33x at rho=0.5 and 1.96x at rho=0.7. Dorner et al. (ICLR 2025) show that a proxy weaker than the evaluated system cannot save more than half of the gold labels. (3) The regression also ignores errors in variables (noisy cheap means pull b toward 0) and gives no prediction-interval pruning rule. (4) The single available source of pairing is missing: replaying a logged decision context to another model.
errors.correction: Add the missing literature with its applicability limits. State explicitly that episode-level control variates, PPI and MFMC between actors are inapplicable. Use a policy-level random-effects model with residual SD tau, and prune only through predictive intervals that include the upper bound on tau. Apply PPI-style estimators only to population quantities with randomly audited policies. Add decision-level replay as the paired instrument for measuring preference divergence.

recommendations.recommendation: Build an attested, constrained Claude worker harness: empty temp cwd outside the repo and runner directories; --strict-mcp-config with only the official server command and flags copied from make setup; --tools limited to MCP; --system-prompt replacing the default with a JiuwenSwarm-equivalent prompt; plugins and skills disabled; fixed --model and --effort; stream-json init event stored; harness_invalid on any deviation.

recommendations.recommendation: Pre-register cheap-actor license levels. L0 (default): cheap scores may only reorder the queue. L1 (coarse pruning, per family stratum): allowed only when execution parity, preference divergence, rho_true and residual-complexity criteria all hold. L2 (selection or promotion on cheap scores): never. Pruning under L1 uses a predictive interval that includes the upper bound on tau.
recommendations.rationale: This turns the 'if the relation is bad' language into checkable rules, controls repeated looks (two scheduled looks with alpha split), and makes 'fidelity not established' a safe default rather than a stall.

recommendations.recommendation: Separate the three failure modes with three instruments. Execution: per-decision compliance and tool-error metrics from trajectories, with episode-cluster bootstrap CIs. Preference: decision-level replay of identical logged contexts to the cheap actor and to the target itself, with Preference Divergence Index PDI = A_TT - A_CT. Transfer: a policy-level bivariate random-effects model.
recommendations.rationale: Replay is the only paired measurement available without seeds or cloning, and it is cheap (one call per decision). The target's own re-sampling agreement A_TT gives a noise ceiling, so preference bias is distinguished from stochasticity.

recommendations.recommendation: Design the audit of discarded candidates with known inclusion probabilities, Horvitz-Thompson estimators of the mean target gap and false-rejection rate, calibration z-scores and exceedance checks, Holm control across audits, and a revocation rule that re-queues every 'dormant_cheap' candidate in the stratum.
recommendations.rationale: Per-candidate audits with 2-3 episodes are too noisy to classify individual rejections. Pooled estimators with known probabilities are unbiased and informative.

recommendations.recommendation: Extend records.schema.json with an actor_config object, a compliance block, interruption_cause and an 'official_evaluation' execution class. Add actor and harness fields to experiment-registry.json.
recommendations.rationale: Without these fields the required policy x actor x environment separation cannot be recorded.

recommendations.recommendation: Size the calibration matrix from observed variability: K=10 pre-registered policies (2 anchors plus 8 candidates from at least 4 families, at least 2 long or complex), 2 episodes per cell on target and on Haiku, then top up to n* = ceil(2.33 sigma_T^2 / s_b^2) if n* <= 4. Otherwise stop at L0. Report every statistic with and without the anchors.
recommendations.rationale: Anchors widen the range and inflate correlation (spectrum bias). The decision-relevant quantity is residual tau among top candidates.

recommendations.recommendation: Use policy-level PPI++ or stratified PPI only for population estimands, for example the mean target score of candidates produced by a generator, family or reopening operator in a round. Cheap predictions must be cross-fitted from earlier rounds. State that the effective-sample-size gain is at most 1/(1-rho^2), and that episode-level PPI, control variates and MFMC between actors give no gain.
recommendations.rationale: This supports ablations such as 'reopening produces better candidates' without overclaiming what PPI can do.

recommendations.recommendation: Use Sonnet or Opus as an oracle executor for diagnosis only, never as a selection arm. Add cheap target-model comprehension probes for each Skill (restate the rule, apply it to 5 public-information vignettes) as a covariate and a pre-filter for execution capability.
recommendations.rationale: The capability direction is unknown, and stronger actors may mask under-specified Skills. Probes test executability on the actual target at almost no cost.

recommendations.recommendation: Measure token efficiency (tokens per month survived) only on the target configuration and include it in candidate comparisons as an auxiliary metric.
recommendations.rationale: It is 10% of the automated score and cannot be calibrated from Claude harnesses.

recommendations.recommendation: Handle subscription interruptions explicitly: keep the server alive independently of the actor (http transport only after organiser approval), resume instead of restarting, record interruption causes, and test whether interruptions concentrate in long episodes.
recommendations.rationale: Length-biased censoring would bias Claude-cell means toward short, failing episodes.
evidence: Task context: Max plan, extra usage disabled; CLI --transport options

recommendations.recommendation: Log each official 3-run release as a separate eval-environment cell and compute z = (Qbar_official - ybar_dev) / sqrt(sigma^2/3 + sigma^2/n_dev) for the same frozen version.
recommendations.rationale: These are the only target observations on the closed evaluation dataset. They detect dev-to-eval shift but must not be pooled with dev data.
evidence: scratchpad/docs/competition-rules.rst.txt 'Which version is evaluated'; 'closed evaluation dataset'

recommendations.rationale: Without a common unit the 'cheap sources save cost' comparison is undefined.

audit.concrete_protocol:
Calibration protocol for problem A (worker capability and bias). All numbers are laboratory parameters, not game rules.

0. ACTOR = CONFIGURATION
An actor a is a tuple: served model version (and observable provider/quantization mix), route/key class, harness and version, system-prompt hash, Skill-loading mode, reasoning/effort setting, context policy (compaction or truncation), exact MCP server command and flags (including -c and transport), and dataset split. Statistics are kept per (policy sha256 x a x environment epoch). Extend records.schema.json to match.

1. ACTOR LADDER
- A0 Official: 3 runs per scored version on the closed evaluation dataset. Used only as an environment-shift check; never pooled with dev data.
- A1 Gold-dev: JiuwenSwarm 0.2.4b3, mode agent, competition key, MODEL_NAME exactly as emailed, dev split, MCP command as written by make setup.
- A2 Near-gold (needs the user's budget approval and an organiser reply): identical to A1 but with a team-funded OpenRouter key and slug deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (on 26 Oct this is 'V4 Flash 0423', 17 endpoints, fp4/fp8/mxfp4). Default routing, no provider preferences, served provider logged from OpenRouter activity. Not DeepSeek's first-party API, which serves V4.1-Flash-1017 under the legacy name.
  - Pool A2 with A1 only if both hold: (i) replay agreement A(A2 vs A1 contexts) >= A_TT(A1) - 0.05; (ii) the episode-mean difference lies within +/- Delta_min by TOST at 80%. Otherwise keep A2 as a separate source calibrated to A1.
- A3 (optional): same OpenRouter model inside the constrained Claude Code harness, to measure the harness effect.
- B1: Haiku 5.5 in the constrained, attested Claude Code harness.
- B2: Sonnet 5.5 in the same harness, as an oracle executor for diagnosis only.
- S (if organiser question A2 is approved): scripted deterministic actor, for environment variance and as a negative control.
- Constrained harness requirements:
  - empty temp cwd, no access to the repo, .career_sim_runner, the database or packages;
  - --strict-mcp-config with only the official server;
  - --tools limited to MCP; --system-prompt replaced;
  - plugins and skills off; fixed --model and --effort;
  - stream-json output with the init event stored (any extra tool or skill makes the episode harness_invalid);
  - compaction events logged.

2. STAGES (variability-driven; two scheduled looks)
- Step 0 (pilot):
  - 2 A1 episodes and 2 B1 episodes of one minimal policy; 20-30 S episodes if allowed.
  - Outputs: $/episode, tokens/month, wall-clock, subscription usage per episode, sigma_env.
  - Prior bracket, to be replaced by the measurement: about 200 decisions and at least 400 turns per game; 10^7-10^8 input tokens if history is retained; about $0.3-8 per target episode; the key buys roughly 6-150 episodes.
- Step 1 (core matrix, pre-registered before any result):
  - K = 10 frozen policies: 2 anchors (a minimal general procedure, and a valid but deliberately weak one such as 'ignore wellbeing warnings') plus 8 candidates from at least 4 families, at least 2 of them long or complex.
  - n = 2 episodes per cell on the target (A2 if approved, else A1) and on B1: 20 + 20 episodes. Interleave actors and policies in randomized order within the same time windows.
  - Replay: from every target episode, sample 30 decisions stratified by type (story / Energy / main) x month tercile.
    - Query B1 once with the identical context text and no tools, and record its choice.
    - Re-query the target once (self-consistency A_TT).
    - Reverse direction: from each B1 episode, replay 30 decisions to the target.
- Step 2 (top-up):
  - From Step 1, estimate the pooled within-cell SD sigma_hat_T and the between-policy SD s_hat_b (REML).
  - Compute n* = ceil(2.33 * sigma_hat_T^2 / s_hat_b^2), which gives reliability R = 0.7.
  - If n* <= 4 and budget allows, top up the target cells to n* (and B1 likewise). Otherwise stop: the license stays L0.
  - License decisions use alpha/2 at each of the two looks.
- New family: starts at L0. It is eligible for L1 after at least 3 of its policies have cells on both actors and the family's standardized residuals all satisfy |z| < 2.

3. STATISTICS
(1) Execution capability: rates per 100 decisions of
  - invalid or unavailable choice attempts;
  - unaffordable Energy attempts;
  - tool errors;
  - blind retry after an ambiguous take_action;
  - loop abandonment before the terminal state (operational failure, not game elimination);
  - missing notes;
  - policy-checklist violations, judged by Opus on sampled decisions. The judge is validated on 50 hand-labelled decisions and is used only if accuracy >= 0.85.
  Report episode-cluster bootstrap 90% CIs and the ratio C/T.
(2) Preference/bias:
  - A_CT = share of replayed contexts where the cheap actor's choice equals the target's choice.
  - PDI = A_TT - A_CT, with cluster-bootstrap CIs, per decision type.
  - Directional profile: share of choices with wellbeing-protective vs growth published direction, per actor, on identical contexts.
(3) Transfer: fit the bivariate errors-in-variables random-effects model
  - ybar_{p,a} = mu_{p,a} + e, Var(e) = sigma_a^2 / n_{p,a};
  - mu_{p,T} = alpha + beta * mu_{p,C} + u_p, u_p ~ N(0, tau^2), optionally with a family effect.
  Report:
  - rho_true, beta and tau with 80% and 95% intervals;
  - Kendall tau_b of the cell means, with a two-level bootstrap (episodes within cells, then policies);
  - top-3 recall and expected target regret of the cheap top-1, by posterior simulation;
  - compression ratio s_b,C / s_b,T;
  - regression of the residual on complexity and family (input-dependent fidelity);
  - all of the above with and without the anchors.
Do NOT use episode-level control variates, PPI or MFMC between actors: the episodes are unpaired, so they give zero gain.
Policy-level PPI++ (stratified by family; cheap prediction cross-fitted from earlier rounds) is used only for population estimands, such as the mean target score of a generator's candidates in a round. Expected effective-sample-size gain is at most 1/(1-rho^2): 1.33x at rho=0.5, 1.96x at rho=0.7.

4. LICENSE AND PRUNING RULES (per family stratum, pre-registered)
- L0 (default): cheap results may reorder the queue. They never make a valid policy dormant and never promote one.
- L1 (coarse pruning) requires all of:
  - (a) execution parity: the C/T violation ratio lies in [0.5, 2], or both rates are below 2 per 100 decisions;
  - (b) PDI upper 80% bound <= 0.15;
  - (c) rho_true lower 80% bound >= 0.5 (break-even in simulation at s_b=5, sigma=15; recompute the break-even with the observed sigma and s_b before applying);
  - (d) residual-complexity slope |t| < 2;
  - (e) at least 3 policies from the family in the matrix.
- Pruning under L1:
  - Predicted target mean m_i = alpha_hat + beta_hat * ybar_{i,C}.
  - s_i^2 = beta_hat^2 * sigma_C^2 / n_{i,C} + tau_U^2 + parameter variance, where tau_U is the upper 80% bound of tau.
  - Make candidate i 'dormant_cheap' if and only if P(mu_{i,T} >= mu_{inc,T} - Delta_min) < 0.10, i.e. (m_i - ybar_inc,T + Delta_min) / sqrt(s_i^2 + SE_inc^2) < -1.28.
  - Delta_min = 3 quantitative points (2.4 automated points), pre-registered.
  - Equivalent multi-fidelity best-arm form: eliminate i if UCB_C(i) + xi < LCB_C(inc) - xi, with xi = 1.28 * sqrt(2) * tau_U / |beta_hat|.
- L2 (selection or promotion on cheap scores): never. Promotion uses only A1/A2 episodes. The final choice requires a frozen, fresh A1 confirmation batch.

5. AUDITS OF DISCARDED CANDIDATES
- Each 'dormant_cheap' candidate i is audited with probability pi_i = clip(0.2 + 4 * P_i, 0.2, 1), drawn with a logged seeded RNG and stored in its record. Audit = 2 target episodes.
- Estimators:
  - Horvitz-Thompson mean gap: G_hat = (1/N) * sum over audited (ybar_{i,T} - ybar_inc) / pi_i.
  - Calibration z-scores: z_i = (ybar_{i,T} - m_i) / sqrt(s_i^2 + sigma_T^2 / 2).
  - Exceedance rate above the predictive 90% upper bound (expected 10%).
  - HT false-rejection rate of 1[ybar_{i,T} >= ybar_inc - Delta_min], reported as noisy.
- Revoke L1 for the stratum if any of these holds:
  - mean z > 0 at one-sided alpha = 0.10;
  - the binomial lower bound of the exceedance rate is > 0.10;
  - the false-rejection rate's upper 80% bound is > 0.20;
  - any audited candidate beats the incumbent by more than Delta_min with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05.
  On revocation, every 'dormant_cheap' candidate in the stratum returns to the queue.

6. BUDGET AND SCHEDULE
- Competition key:
  - Reserve >= 40% for frozen confirmation of 1-2 finalists on A1 (for example 8-10 episodes each).
  - If A2 is unavailable, use <= 35% for calibration target cells and audits; the rest goes to spot checks.
  - If A2 is approved, A2 does the screening and calibration bulk; A1 provides anchor cells and the confirmation.
- Claude subscription: schedule within usage windows; keep the server alive across interruptions and resume; record the interruption cause; compare interruption rates by survival month (Kaplan-Meier-style) to detect length-biased censoring.
- A0: after each release compute z = (Qbar_official - ybar_A1) / sqrt(sigma^2 / 3 + sigma^2 / n_A1).

7. METHOD EVALUATION
- Budget unit: target episodes (A1 + A2) plus wall-clock time; Claude usage reported separately.
- Arms:
  - (i) target-only successive halving;
  - (ii) cheap screening under L1 rules with audits;
  - (iii) cheap screening without the gate;
  - (iv) gate without audits.
- Metrics:
  - regret of the selected policy on a fresh A1 confirmation batch;
  - audited false-rejection rate;
  - target episodes saved;
  - wall-clock time.
- The unit of replication is a whole search. A single search is reported as a pilot.
failure_evidence: The PDI CI excludes 0 with PDI > 0.15, or the directional choice profile on identical contexts differs systematically between the cheap actor and the target.
The lower 80% bound of rho_true is below the recomputed break-even (about 0.5), the beta_hat CI includes 0, or the compression ratio s_b,C/s_b,T is below 0.5.
Audited cheap-pruned candidates show mean calibration z > 0, an exceedance rate above 10%, or an HT false-rejection rate whose upper bound exceeds 20%.
Calibration residuals correlate with Skill length or complexity, or with family (input-dependent fidelity), especially for specialists.
Candidates promoted on cheap evidence fail fresh A1 confirmation twice in a row.
Execution metrics diverge: the target's tool-error or invalid-action rate is more than twice the cheap actor's, or vice versa.
A2 differs from A1 (outside equivalence margins), the served provider mix shifts, or the slug's dated version changes mid-week.
Harness attestation failures appear, or compaction events and subscription interruptions concentrate in long, high-survival episodes.
Target tokens per month are far from what the pilot or the Claude harness suggested, so efficiency-term rankings flip.
The official A0 mean falls outside the dev prediction interval for the same frozen version (dev-to-eval shift).

verdicts.reason: Partly confirmed. protocol.md lines 17-23 and lab-spec.json lines 92-113 price only the three Claude models and never price the target. I re-fetched the OpenRouter endpoint list: it has 17 endpoints, named 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0423'. Prompt prices run 5e-8 to 6e-7 USD/token (most 0.08-0.15 $/M), completion 1.65e-7 to 1.32e-6, and cache reads mostly 0.014-0.07 $/M. The Anthropic Haiku page confirms $0.10/$0.50 up to 100K and $0.50/$2.50 above. So per token the target is not dearer than Haiku. The prior's own framing ('Trabajador barato', USD gate external_spending_limit_usd) assumed API billing and never compared against the target. Overclaims in the auditor: (a) 'will exceed 100k tokens per request' depends on compaction; careerlab/actors/claude_cli.py already has an autocompact option (e.g. '100k'). (b) 'would remove most of the reason for low-fidelity screening' is contradicted by the auditor's own budget.py, which I re-ran. At equal target budget (24 episodes, K=12), cheap screening lowers regret from 3.9 (target-only successive halving) to 2.7-3.4 at rho 0.7-0.9. Under a subscription, Claude episodes cost no marginal USD, so they keep value whenever rho is at least about 0.5. (c) The prior was not wrong to treat the target as scarce. Without an approved team-funded route, the only target source is the USD 50 key; the prior's organiser-questions.md Q6 assumes all representative games use that key.
verdicts.refined_correction: Price and time the target before designing anything else: measure tokens, $ and wall-clock for 1-2 target episodes. Replace the USD price table with three cost units: target $ per episode, Claude subscription usage per episode, and wall-clock. Make the ladder conditional. If team-funded target access (same OpenRouter slug, same JiuwenSwarm setup) is approved by both the user and the organisers, the target becomes the default scoring actor. If it is not approved, the target stays scarce (USD 50) and Claude workers remain the zero-marginal-USD source. In both cases Claude scores may reorder the queue but gain pruning authority only through an explicit calibration license. Drop the claim that a funded target 'removes most of the reason' for screening: the gain depends on rho and on the target budget.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. protocol.md lines 53-63 and mathematics.md lines 102-110 name diagnostics but give no estimator, threshold or decision rule. They say only 'si el acuerdo es insuficiente'. I re-ran fidelity.py and the numbers are right: Fisher-z 95% CI for r=0.8 is [-0.03, 0.98] at K=6, [0.42, 0.94] at K=12 and [0.55, 0.92] at K=20. Reliability of cell means is 0.16 (s_b=5, sigma=20, n=3) and 0.75 (10, 10, 3). The n* formula 2.33*sigma^2/s_b^2 for R=0.7 is algebraically correct. Mitigation in the prior: it labels the pilot 'not a power justification' and defaults to 'fidelidad no establecida' if the matrix is cut. That is a safe default, not a gate. The task explicitly requires pre-registered numeric criteria.
verdicts.refined_correction: Pre-register numeric license criteria and a default of no pruning. Before running the matrix, also simulate the probability of reaching the pruning license under plausible (s_b, sigma, rho) values. At s_b=5 and sigma=15, n* = 21, and even a perfectly measured r=0.8 at K=10 has an 80% lower bound of only about 0.55. If that probability is low, do not spend the target budget on a calibration matrix: run target-only selection and use Claude cells only for queue ordering and diagnosis. Use an errors-in-variables / bivariate random-effects fit rather than a raw correlation, and report results with and without anchors.

verdicts.reason: Partly confirmed. Verified: Optimal MF-BAI (arXiv 2406.03033) states 'We assume that the algorithm knows both the cost and the maximal bias of the observations from each fidelity'. The Kandasamy and Poiani 2022 settings likewise assume known bias bounds. This bias-bound literature is missing from bibliography.md, and the known-bias assumption is the key applicability limit. The errors-in-variables gap is real: mathematics.md line 96 gives no estimator, and regressing on noisy cheap means attenuates b. Decision-level replay is a genuinely missing paired instrument. Overstatements: (a) 'the literature that actually governs this decision is missing' ignores what the bibliography already has. R34 (Poloczek et al. MISO, which models source bias with a GP and needs no known bound) and R36-R38 (top-two BAI, confidence sequences) are both present. (b) PPI, control variates and MFMC were never proposed by the prior, so their inapplicability is an addition, not a correction. (c) Lumping Kennedy-O'Hagan co-kriging with the inapplicable episode-level methods is misleading. KOH (f_T = rho*f_C + delta over inputs) is exactly the policy-level calibration model the prior wrote, so it applies with policies as inputs. (d) Dorner et al. (arXiv 2410.13341) is about LLM judges labelling the same items: 'when the judge is no more accurate than the evaluated model, no debiasing method can decrease the required amount of ground truth labels by more than half'. It is an analogy here, not a direct bound. The 1/(1-rho^2) PPI++ ceiling is correct in the N>>n limit.
verdicts.refined_correction: Add the multi-fidelity best-arm literature (Kandasamy 2016; Poiani 2022, 2024), stating that it assumes known per-fidelity bias bounds, so the lab must estimate an upper bound on tau and carry its uncertainty. Present the prior's calibration as a KOH / MISO-style policy-level model fitted with errors-in-variables, with pruning only through predictive intervals that include tau. State that episode-level control variates, PPI and MFMC between unpaired actors give no gain. Cite PPI++ only for policy-population estimands, and Dorner et al. only as an analogy. Add decision-level replay as the paired diagnostic, conditional on being able to extract the exact contexts.

Length-biased censoring is plausible. careerlab/actors/claude_cli.py shows how it would arise: rate-limit errors end claude -p, and the loop immediately re-prompts up to max_continues=3, then labels the episode 'game not finished after 3 continuations'.
